title: apricity-daw export planning: write, unchanged, skipped or refused per sample
description:
## Intent
The pure planning step: given samples, decide what to write and why, with no I/O beyond reading.

## Scope
- `crates/apricity-daw/src/export.rs`: `plan_sample_sidecar(clip: &apricity_score::Clip, audio: &Path, existing: Option<&[u8]>, force: bool) -> Outcome` where `Outcome` ∈ `Write(bytes) | Unchanged | Skipped(reason) | Refused(reason)`.
- Rules: stale sha256 → Refused; no beat grid → Write unwarped; existing sidecar equal to the grid (within 0.1 ms / 0.001 beat) → Unchanged; different and not `force` → Refused with the import hint; writes `.asd` on M0 go, `.alc` otherwise.
- Unit tests for each branch.

## Verify
`safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-daw export`.

Commit: `feat(<this id>): plan sample sidecars`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
